terms.gloss: it concerns, it has to do with
terms.grammar: verb: third person of attineō, with ad and the accusative
evidence: Plaut. Trin. 1065: quid id ad mē attinet?
terms.comment: Quod ad mē attinet, as far as I am concerned (Cic. Q. fr. 2.1, Att. 5.17, Lewis & Short). Often shortened: istae quid ad mē?, what have these to do with me? (Plaut. Pers. 497).

terms.grammar: verb: third person of pertineō, with ad and the accusative
evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 36: illa rēs ad meum officium pertinet (Lewis & Short)

terms.grammar: impersonal verb, with meā, tuā or a genitive
terms.comment: Interest is used the same way: meā interest, it matters to me (Traupman 302).

phrases.english: what has that to do with me?

phrases.latin: Istae quid ad mē? — Immō ad tē attinent et tuā rēfert.
phrases.english: What have these to do with me? — Oh, they concern you, and it matters to you.

phrases.latin: tantumne est ab rē tuā ōtī tibi, aliēna ut cūrēs eaque nihil quae ad tē attinent?
phrases.english: have you so much time to spare from your own affairs that you look after other people’s, which don’t concern you?

phrases.latin: nam tua rēs agitur, pariēs cum proximus ārdet
phrases.english: for it is your concern when the wall next door is on fire

sources: Lewis & Short: attineo · Lewis & Short: pertineo · Lewis & Short: refert
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 294, 302, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).

Quotations of Plautus (Leo, 1896; cited by his lines), Terence (Parry, 1857; cited by the lines of the Oxford text) and Horace (Fairclough, 1929) that are not in the loci collections were checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
